commit.message:
Desktop: a failed turn says why, not "Internal error" (#89)

## What and why

A failed chat turn often showed only "Internal error". In #81 the real
cause was that the model service sent nothing for 5 minutes, three
times; the person had no way to tell.

The cause was lost in two places:

- **Our own agent** (`pi-agent.mjs`) threw plain Errors. The ACP SDK
turns a plain thrown Error into `{ code: -32603, message: "Internal
error", data: { details: "<the real text>" } }` (`errorToResult` in
`@agentclientprotocol/sdk`), and the chat showed `message`.
- **The client** read the reason from `data` only when a session
started, not during a turn. Codex, for one, sends "Internal error" with
its reason in `data`.

Now:

- `pi-agent.mjs` throws the SDK's `RequestError` with the real text, so
our agent's errors arrive as they are. Pi's raw words go along in
`data.details` when the shown text is reworded.
- `errorCause()` in `agents.mjs` shows the reason from `data` (a string,
`message` or `details`) when an error is exactly -32603 "Internal
error". This applies to every ACP agent, at session start and during
turns.
- `failureText()` in `pi-config.mjs` rewords two technical cases.
Everything else is shown as the service said it.
- "Request timed out." → "The model service didn't answer for 5 minutes,
even after retries. Check that the service is running and reachable,
then try again."
- context overflow → "The conversation is too long for the model. The
model's context may be smaller than set in Settings: lower it there."
(pairs with #88)
- An overflow on the first message used to end the turn silently,
because Pi drops the failed answer. The turn's last answer now comes
from Pi's own events, so it fails with the reason.
- The turn log keeps the error as the agent sent it (`code`, `message`,
`data`).

"terminated" and "Connection error." are left as Pi says them: they can
mean a dropped or refused connection, not only a timeout.

## Testing

- New tests in `agents.test.mjs` (-32603 with the reason in `data` as a
string, `message`, `details`), `pi-config.test.mjs` (the rewording), and
`pi-agent.test.mjs` against a real local server (a 400 reaches the chat
with its own text; overflow).
- Checked the timeout text by running Pi against a server that never
answers: Pi says exactly "Request timed out.".
- `pnpm typecheck` passes; desktop tests 202/202; `pnpm audit:public`
clean.

A `patch` changeset is included.
